messages:
Jo: Quick weekend poll: if you could bring only one board game to a desert-island-style retreat, which one and why? Keep it practical or chaos-optimized.
Ravi: Codenames  short rounds, easy to teach, and groups of odd sizes are OK.
Sana: Ticket to Ride  long-ish but great for bonding and accidental rivalries.
Tess: Sushi Go!  fast, adorable, and you can play 100 rounds in an afternoon.
Jo: @office-bot run a tiny poll?
office-bot: Poll created: "Pick one board game for desert retreat"  Options: Codenames / Ticket to Ride / Sushi Go! / Other
Ravi: Vote cast: Codenames :speech_balloon:
Sana: Vote cast: Ticket to Ride :train2:
Tess: Vote cast: Sushi Go! :sushi:
Jo: Voted Other ("A deck of blank index cards to invent games on the spot")
Ravi: Blank cards are actually genius. Infinite replayability.
Sana: If Ticket to Ride wins I will bring a printable map and extra colored pens.
Tess: If Sushi Go! wins I will craft tiny cardboard sushi tokens for ceremony.
Jo: Whoever voted Other owes us a one-line pitch for a new card game idea.
office-bot: Reminder set: "Board game prototyping session" Friday 5pm in lounge.
Ravi: Low-effort, high-joy. Also, dessert and game night?
Sana: I'll bring the biscuits. Tess: you bring sushi tokens. Jo: bring enthusiasm.
Tess: Deal. Also someone remind me to bring a tiny timer.
Jo: Thread wrap: post your one-line game pitch in this thread if you voted Other. Prize: eternal bragging rights.
Ravi: I'll prototype a one-card-version of Codenames that we can play on the beach.
Sana: Can't wait.
